reasons: The honesty rules are clearly tested, but no test run result was provided.
The route tests rely on stubbed network calls, not the real outside service.

terms.meaning: A ranking of how much each kind of data source is trusted.
Data that is old enough that it should not be shown as current.
A record of where a value came from and when it was observed.
A recorded past match shown as if it were happening again.

used_by: Run by the test runner as part of the unit tests.

sections.name: File setup, at, src, live
sections.title: Test setup and fixed clock
sections.what: Imports the test runner, the source choice and format functions, the priority table and the type. Sets a fixed time and small helpers that make sourced values with a chosen age, plus a live context.
sections.why: A fixed time keeps ages and labels the same on every run.
sections.watch_out: Fixed time means these tests do not check the real clock.

sections.name: authority: source priority and honest labels
sections.title: Source choice and honest labels
sections.what: Checks the priority table, that the freshest high-priority source is chosen, that a stale high-priority source is skipped for a fresh lower one, that a stale fallback is labelled with its age, that simulated and projected data are never labelled live, that nothing is live while live calls are off or for delayed sources, that replays are labelled as replays and missing sources as pending, and that ages are formatted in seconds, minutes, hours or days.
sections.why: Likely reason: the live label is the app's core honesty promise, so these rules are checked in detail.
sections.watch_out: An error in these rules could present old or simulated numbers as live.

sections.name: authority: live-score route
sections.title: Checks the live score route's data labels
sections.what: Runs the live score endpoint with a fake third-party response and checks that the data is labelled Delayed, not Live, and that the run rate is worked out correctly. A second check confirms that with no API key the endpoint reports the source as pending and returns status 503 instead of making up scores.
sections.why: The third-party feed is not licensed for live use, so the app must never call it live. The tests guard that rule and the rule against inventing data.
sections.watch_out: The test name says a stale label is used as a fallback, but this block does not test that fallback, so it may be an over-claim.

summary: Tests how the app chooses which data source to show and how it labels that data as live, delayed, stale, replay or pending.
purpose: Makes sure the app shows the most trusted fresh source, never labels old or simulated data as live, and never invents a score.
why: Likely reason: users trust the live label, so a mislabelled old or simulated figure would mislead them.
how: Checks the source priority table, then tests choosing the freshest highest-priority source, skipping stale sources when fresh ones exist, showing the newest stale value with its age when nothing is fresh, never labelling simulated or projected data as live, and labelling replays and missing sources. Then tests the live-score route with and without a key.
inputs: Sample sourced values with timestamps and a fixed clock, plus a stubbed outside service response.
outputs: The chosen value, its state, its label and its receipt, plus route responses.
risks: Any error in the live rule can show old data as current. The network and environment stubs must be cleared after each test.
debug: Check the state and label of the chosen value. Compare the age of the value with the freshness limit. For the route, check the key setting and the stubbed response.
